sections.visa: Many nationalities -- including most EU countries, the UK, the US, Canada, and Australia -- can enter Japan visa-free for short tourist stays (typically up to 90 days), though exact allowances vary by passport. Travelers should have a valid passport with sufficient remaining validity and often a return/onward ticket.
sections.best_time_to_visit: Spring (March-May) is popular for cherry blossoms, with mild temperatures. Autumn (September-November) offers similarly mild weather and autumn foliage. Summer (June-August) is hot and humid with a rainy season in June. Winter (December-February) is cool and dry, generally the least crowded season.
sections.local_customs: Bowing is a common greeting. Tipping is not customary and can even cause confusion. It's considered polite to be quiet on trains and to remove shoes when entering homes and certain traditional accommodations. Queuing in an orderly fashion is expected everywhere.
sections.packing_tips: Layered clothing works well given seasonal variation. Comfortable walking shoes are essential given how much travel is done on foot and via train stations. In summer, light breathable fabrics and a portable fan or cooling towel help with humidity; in winter, warm layers are needed as many older buildings are not centrally heated.
sections.safety_notes: Japan is generally considered very safe with low crime rates. The main natural hazards are occasional earthquakes and, during typhoon season (roughly August-October), heavy rain and strong winds. Tap water is safe to drink in most areas.

sections.visa: Iceland is part of the Schengen Area. Visitors from the EU, UK, US, Canada, and Australia typically do not need a visa for short stays (usually up to 90 days within a 180-day period), though rules for non-Schengen visitors vary and should be checked based on nationality.
sections.best_time_to_visit: Summer (June-August) offers mild temperatures and near-midnight sun, ideal for outdoor activities. Winter (December-February) is cold with very short daylight hours but is the best season for viewing the Northern Lights. Shoulder seasons (spring/autumn) offer fewer crowds but more unpredictable weather.
sections.local_customs: Icelanders are generally informal; first names are used often, even in professional settings. Tipping is not expected, as service charges are typically included. Punctuality is valued. Outdoor hot tub/pool etiquette requires showering (without swimwear) before entering.
sections.packing_tips: Weather can change rapidly regardless of season, so waterproof and windproof outer layers are strongly recommended year-round. Warm layers, a hat, and gloves are essential in winter. Sturdy waterproof footwear is recommended for exploring natural sites such as waterfalls and glaciers.
sections.safety_notes: Iceland is considered very safe with very low crime rates. The main risks are weather and terrain related -- sudden storms, icy roads in winter, and unpredictable conditions near cliffs, glaciers, and hot springs. It's advisable to check road and weather conditions before day trips outside Reykjavik.

sections.visa: Many nationalities, including most EU countries, the UK, the US, Canada, and Australia, can enter Thailand visa-free or via visa-on-arrival for stays typically up to 30 days, though this varies by nationality and is subject to change. Travelers should check current requirements for their specific passport.
sections.best_time_to_visit: The cool season (November-February) is generally considered the most comfortable, with lower humidity. The hot season (March-May) brings high temperatures. The rainy season (June-October) brings monsoon rains, often in short, heavy bursts rather than all-day rain.
sections.local_customs: Thailand places strong cultural importance on respect for the monarchy and Buddhist traditions; visitors should dress modestly when visiting temples (shoulders and knees covered) and remove shoes before entering. Public displays of anger are frowned upon, and the head is considered a sacred part of the body (avoid touching others' heads), while feet are considered the lowest/least respectful (avoid pointing feet at people or religious images).
sections.packing_tips: Lightweight, breathable clothing is recommended given the heat and humidity. A modest cover-up layer (long trousers/skirt, a shoulder-covering top) is useful for temple visits. A compact umbrella or rain jacket is handy during the rainy season.
sections.safety_notes: Bangkok is generally safe for tourists, though petty theft and common tourist scams occur in busy areas. Tap water is generally not recommended for drinking; bottled or filtered water is preferred. Traffic can be heavy and pedestrian crossings should be navigated carefully.

sections.visa: Spain is part of the Schengen Area. Visitors from the EU, UK, US, Canada, and Australia typically do not need a visa for short tourist stays (usually up to 90 days within a 180-day period); requirements for other nationalities vary.
sections.best_time_to_visit: Late spring (May-June) and early autumn (September-October) offer warm, pleasant weather without the peak summer crowds and heat. Summer (July-August) is hot and the most crowded/tourist-heavy season. Winter is mild compared to much of Europe but can be cool and occasionally rainy.
sections.local_customs: Meal times run later than in many countries -- lunch is often early-to-mid afternoon and dinner frequently after 9 pm. A short rest period ("siesta") in the early afternoon is a cultural norm, though less universally observed in tourist areas. A modest, included service charge is common, though small additional tips for good service are appreciated but not obligatory.
sections.packing_tips: Comfortable walking shoes are recommended given how walkable the city is. Light layers work well for most of the year; a light jacket is useful for cooler evenings even in summer. Modest attire (shoulders covered) is expected when visiting churches such as the Sagrada Familia.
sections.safety_notes: Barcelona is generally safe but has a notable rate of pickpocketing and bag-snatching in tourist-heavy areas (public transport, Las Ramblas, beaches). Keeping valuables secure and being alert in crowds is commonly advised. Tap water is safe to drink.
